sections.heading: Core Gameplay Mechanics
sections.body:
At its core, Ghosts Memory Match is a tile-matching game. Players are presented with a grid of tiles, each bearing a piece of a larger picture. The objective is to slide the tiles around until the complete image is revealed. Sounds simple, but don't be fooled - the game's increasing difficulty and complex mechanics make it a true challenge. One of the key features that sets Ghosts Memory Match apart from other puzzle games is its use of a 'ghost' tile. This tile is a permanent fixture in the game board, and serves as a reference point for players to match their tiles against. It's a clever touch that adds depth and complexity to the game without overwhelming the player.

The game's controls are intuitive and easy to use, making it accessible to players of all ages and skill levels. Players can use their mouse, keyboard, or touch controls to slide the tiles around. The game also features a handy undo feature, which allows players to revert to a previous state if they make a mistake. This is a lifesaver, trust us - you'll be using it more often than you think.

As players progress through the game, the tiles become increasingly complex. Some tiles may have multiple pieces, or may be hidden behind other tiles. This adds a whole new level of strategy to the game, as players must carefully plan their moves to maximize their chances of success.
